title: Causal checkpoint & resume fingerprint for interrupted streaming generations
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Customers running long-form streaming generations see inconsistent outputs or duplicate tokens when clients disconnect and later reconnect to resume. Root causes: non-deterministic KV cache state (prefix/cached activations), lack of a compact resumable fingerprint, and missing durable tombstones for partially emitted token ranges. This ticket proposes a causal checkpointing scheme: emit lightweight, cryptographic resume fingerprints tied to causal model state (prefix hash + kv-version + generation-offset) and persist a compact tombstone when a session is aborted. Fingerprint + tombstone semantics allow safe resume on compatible model/runtime variants and provide an audit trail for debugging and SLO reconciliation.
acceptance_criteria: Server emits a resume_fingerprint header at stable checkpoints during streaming generations (every ~64 tokens or KB-based boundary).
Resume fingerprint encodes: model_id:version, kv_cache_version, prefix_digest, generation_offset, and server_epoch; fingerprint size < 256 bytes in base64 and verifiable by server.
On client reconnect with a resume_fingerprint, server verifies compatibility and either accepts resume (fast-path) or returns a deterministic graceful-fallback response explaining incompatibility.

Aborted generations create a tombstone record with a TTL and audit metadata (reason, client_id, last_offset). Tombstones prevent accidental replay or duplicate token emission for the same logical generation.
End-to-end unit + integration tests exercising disconnect, reconnect, incompatible-model upgrade, and tombstone GC are added.
Metrics: resume_success_rate, resume_latency_delta, tombstone_count, tombstone_gc_latency added to runtime telemetry dashboards.
tasks: Design resume_fingerprint protobuf schema and base64 envelope (Aisha)
Update serving runtime to compute prefix_digest deterministically from tokenized prefix and KV meta (Marco)
Emit fingerprint on stable checkpoints and include in streaming frames and metadata endpoints (runtime + SDK changes)
Implement tombstone write path into ephemeral metadata store with TTL and audit fields
Add verification logic for resume requests that compares fingerprint components and applies compatibility policy
Add extensive tests and chaos scenarios in staging (disconnect at random offsets, service restart, model swap)
design_notes: Fingerprint composition: sha256(prefix_bytes || kv_version || model_version || server_epoch || offset) signed with server HMAC key to detect tampering; servers accept only current or previous server_epoch to allow rolling upgrades.
We intentionally keep fingerprint deterministic and independent of runtime-specific kernel allocations to maximize portability across dedicated/private deployments.

Tombstones are small JSON records with keys: fingerprint, client_id (anon id), reason (disconnect/timeout/error), last_offset, created_at, ttl_seconds, originating_node. Tombstone GC policy will be conservative (default 24h) and configurable by tenancy.

Compatibility policy: resume allowed if model_id/version matches or model is a verified compatible variant; kv_version must match exactly; if mismatch, server returns a 409 with human-readable guidance and a fast re-run hint (server-provided recommended rewind offset).

To avoid increasing per-token latency, checksum and kv_version computation runs in a background I/O-safe path; checkpoints are opportunistic (every N tokens) and can be forced by SDKs via an 'emit_checkpoint' control frame.
implementation_steps: 1) Propose fingerprint proto and HMAC envelope in design doc and get sign-off (Aisha)
2) Runtime: compute prefix_digest during prefix injection and persist kv_version with checkpoint metadata (Marco + runtime team)
3) API: include resume_fingerprint in streaming frames and in /gen/status endpoints (API team)
4) Metadata store: lightweight tombstone table in existing metadata DB (or redis with persistence) with write/GC APIs (infra team)
5) SDK changes: automatic attach/emit of resume fingerprint on reconnect, and graceful handling of 409 responses with suggested rewind offsets (SDK team)
7) Staged rollout behind feature flag: start on hosted runtime, then Dedicated, then Private with explicit upgrade docs.
rollout_plan: Alpha behind flag: enable on 10% of traffic in runtime-1.22 nightly builds for 48 hours
Smoke tests for resume_success_rate and token-duplication regression, if > 0.1% regress then rollback
Beta: 100% traffic in hosted for non-critical accounts for 2 weeks, monitor tombstone growth and GC behavior
Gradual enablement for Dedicated customers with advisory notices and migration guide
Private: ship as opt-in with CLI migration tooling and administrator controls for tombstone TTL and policies
test_plan: Unit tests: fingerprint generation, HMAC verification, malformed fingerprint handling
Integration: simulated network disconnect at randomized offsets; assert resume accepted when compatible and rejected when incompatible
Chaos: restart serving node mid-generation and validate tombstone creation and resume behavior
Performance: measure checkpoint CPU/latency overhead at 0%, 10%, 100% checkpoint rates; ensure p99 token latency < baseline + 5ms
Security: verify HMAC keys rotate without invalidating recent fingerprints for rolling upgrade window
comments: 2026-02-18 - Aisha: Filed initial spec after customer support escalations reporting duplicated tokens on resume. See attached support excerpts.
2026-02-20 - Marco: Prototype for prefix_digest implemented; using sha256 over bytearray of normalized token ids. Early perf: ~0.6ms per 1KB prefix on p4d. Needs optimization for long prefixes.
2026-02-24 - Priya (SRE): Concern about tombstone write amplification under high disconnect churn; suggested batching tombstone writes and a backpressure limiter for the metadata store.
2026-02-26 - Elena (SDK): We'll add an opt-in 'checkpointOnDemand' flag to allow JS/Go SDKs to force checkpoints after user-visible prompts to reduce resume failure rates for interactive apps.
2026-03-01 - Marco: Added compatibility policy draft — require exact kv_version and allow model_version variants that are registered as compatible in model-catalog. Sending for PM review.

2026-03-04 - Ben (Product): Approved approach; requested telemetry: per-customer resume_failure_reasons and a dashboard for top 10 failure patterns. Also requested rollout playbook for Dedicated tenants.
